title: Aerobic vs anaerobic respiration
examples: What is the main difference between aerobic and anaerobic respiration?
When does lactic acid build up in muscles?
Can you show me the equations for yeast fermentation?

explain.say: Today we are learning about how living things make energy.
Aerobic respiration needs oxygen to release lots of energy.
The word equation shows glucose and oxygen going in.

items: Glucose + Oxygen | Carbon Dioxide + Water + Energy

explain.say: Anaerobic respiration happens without any oxygen present.
In muscles, anaerobic respiration produces lactic acid.
Yeast uses anaerobic respiration to create alcohol and carbon dioxide.

faq.q: Why is aerobic respiration better for making energy?
faq.a: Aerobic respiration breaks down glucose completely using oxygen. This process releases a large amount of usable energy for the cell.
asks: What is the most efficient way to make energy?
Does oxygen help make more energy?

faq.q: What happens to lactic acid when I exercise hard?
faq.a: When you exercise hard, your muscles use anaerobic respiration, which builds up lactic acid. This buildup can cause muscle soreness.
asks: Why do my muscles hurt after running?
Is lactic acid bad for my muscles?

faq.q: How is yeast fermentation different from breathing?
faq.a: Yeast fermentation is a specific form of anaerobic respiration. It is used by yeast to produce alcohol and carbon dioxide gas.

faq.q: What is the chemical equation for aerobic respiration?
faq.a: The balanced equation is glucose plus oxygen yields carbon dioxide, water, and energy.
asks: Can you write the aerobic equation?
What do the reactants and products look like?

faq.q: Does all anaerobic respiration produce lactic acid?
faq.a: No, not all anaerobic respiration produces lactic acid. For example, yeast produces alcohol instead.
asks: Does fermentation always make lactic acid?

facts: Aerobic respiration occurs inside the mitochondria of cells.
The overall equation for aerobic respiration involves glucose and oxygen.
Lactic acid buildup is common during intense, short bursts of exercise.
Yeast fermentation produces ethanol and carbon dioxide gas.

quiz.say: If a cell has plenty of oxygen, which process will it use to get energy?
quiz.why: Aerobic respiration requires oxygen, which is available in plenty.

wrong.0: This is not a recognized biological process for energy release.
wrong.2: This process does not require oxygen, so it would be used when oxygen is low.
wrong.3: Fermentation is a specific type of anaerobic process, not the general choice.

quiz.say: During intense running, the muscle cells might produce lactic acid. This is an example of:
quiz.why: Lactic acid is a byproduct when oxygen supply cannot keep up with energy demand.

wrong.0: Aerobic respiration is the efficient process that uses oxygen.
wrong.1: Yeast fermentation happens in yeast, not human muscle cells.
wrong.2: Photosynthesis makes food, it does not release energy through respiration.

quiz.say: What are the main products when yeast performs fermentation?
quiz.why: Yeast breaks down sugar into these two specific products during fermentation.

wrong.0: This combination is more typical of some other metabolic pathways.
wrong.1: Lactic acid is the product of muscle respiration, not yeast.
wrong.2: Oxygen is a reactant in aerobic respiration, not a product of yeast.
